properties.description: Free-text elaboration of a transferability fact the controlled vocabularies can't capture. Uplifts to `rdfs:comment` on whatever it is attached to.

Identifiers of the artifacts this rule governs, from the enclosing statement's `artifacts`. Several artifacts may share one rule — FP-WF2's four Czechia-specific reference files do. Omit for a rule that applies to the workflow as a whole.
The conditions under which this rule fires, ANDed together. Two conditions here mean both must hold; two rules mean either suffices.

The `id` of an envelope constraint in the enclosing statement's `envelope`, written the same way it is declared there — an IRI, a CURIE, or a bare local name. Whichever form is used, the constraint must still be declared in the statement, so a reader has the extent in front of them rather than a bare identifier: a global identifier makes a boundary shareable, it does not make it fetchable.

How the target is compared against that constraint. `outside` is the condition under which almost every evidenced FOCAL rule fires; `inside` states the complementary case, which is what lets a cascade be written without losing its connecting condition — UP-WF2's "reuse within the domain, otherwise substitute or fail" is two rules over the same constraint. Open vocabulary — see bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.vocab, where each term also records how it is evaluated per dimension.
A coarse statement of what fires this rule, for cases where no envelope constraint can be cited precisely. Open vocabulary — see bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.vocab.
One or more actions, any of which resolves the rule — an OR-set, not a required combination. No evidenced case needs two applied simultaneously.

Whether applying one of `actions` is mandatory once the conditions hold. Defaults to true. When false, skipping is allowed but degrades result quality or trust rather than blocking execution — say what degrades in `transferabilityNotes`.
Named `mandatory` rather than `required`: a data property spelled like a JSON Schema keyword reads as the keyword, and this one sits beside real `required` lists.
